solutions.check: grid and clues read from the FT's printable PDF, its numbering matching the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Peels off in layers

parts.note: reads like fruit or paint coming away, but also suggests a performer removing clothes one garment at a time

explanation.surface: Something flakes away one layer at a time.
explanation.definitionFit: To remove clothing or covering piece by piece is the verb's ordinary sense, and a striptease removes layers.

clue.text: Search thoroughly and flush out

definitions.meaning: to clean by washing water through, as with a pipe

explanation.definitionFit: The verb covers both hunting through a place and scrubbing or rinsing something clean.

clue.text: Umpires have the exclusive right to do this

definitions.text: Umpires have the exclusive right to do this

parts.words: Umpires have the exclusive right to do this
parts.note: an umpire rules a batsman dismissed, and the phrase also means to exclude something

explanation.surface: Only the officials may make this call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exclusive' hints at excluding; in cricket only the umpire may give a batsman out.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to give a player dismissed and to exclude a possibility.

clue.text: Separate layer on ruined Greek temple

parts.note: to part is to separate
a hen is a bird that lays eggs, so a layer
taken as written

explanation.surface: A loose stratum lies on top of an ancient ruin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layer' looks like a stratum but means an egg-laying hen.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous temple of Athena on the Athens Acropolis stands in ruins today.

clue.text: He gives notice, working when others may be playing

definitions.text: He gives notice, working when others may be playing

parts.words: He gives notice, working when others may be playing
parts.note: a reviewer gives a play a notice and works at the theatre while actors are on stage

explanation.surface: A man resigns and works while everyone else is at leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gives notice' suggests quitting a job, but a notice is a review, and 'playing' means acting on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre reviewer writes notices and attends performances as his work.

clue.text: Gathers in spare parts

indicators.note: the word spare is split into parts and its letters reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone collects spare components.
explanation.definitionFit: To reap is to gather in a harvest.

clue.text: Dispensed with red tape and came to the point

indicators.note: dispensed suggests the letters are distributed and laid out afresh

explanation.surface: An official cut bureaucracy and got straight to business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dispensed with' looks like 'did away with'; it is the anagram signal on RED TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tapered narrows to a point at its end.

clue.text: New or ancient vessel

indicators.note: new suggests the letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A ship that may be modern or very old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vessel' tempts one to think of ships, but it is any receptacle.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel in the sense of a receptacle is something that holds contents.

clue.text: Delivery men?

parts.note: suggests couriers, but in cricket a delivery is a ball sent down to the batsman

explanation.surface: People who bring parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket each ball a player sends down is called a delivery.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricketers who send down the ball make deliveries, so they are the delivery men.

clue.text: Up in arms

parts.note: suggests angry protest, but read as a heraldic beast reared up on a coat of arms

explanation.surface: People are furious about something.
explanation.walkthrough: In heraldry a lion standing on its hind legs is described this way; the word also means unchecked and violent.
explanation.definitionFit: A heraldic beast reared upright on its hind legs is so described in a coat of arms.

clue.text: Patricia's in trouble, living at the expense of one's host

definitions.text: living at the expense of one's host

indicators.note: Patricia's letters are in a mess and must be sorted out again

explanation.surface: A woman is having difficulties because she sponges off whoever puts her up.
explanation.definitionFit: A parasite lives off a host organism, and this adjective describes that way of life.

clue.text: The points of quarrels

parts.note: suggests the issues in arguments, but quarrels are also crossbow bolts with sharp tips

explanation.surface: What arguments are really about.
explanation.walkthrough: A quarrel is a short square-headed crossbow bolt.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed tips of missiles such as bolts are their heads.

clue.text: Bring up, or what you may bring up

definitions.meaning: the back of a procession, as in the idiom of coming last

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to raise, and the noun is the back end, which one brings up in the idiom.

clue.text: Stick to external veto

indicators.note: the veto word sits outside, so it wraps around the word to

parts.note: a ban is a veto
taken as written

explanation.surface: Hold firm against a veto from outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like a verb but is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A conductor's or relay runner's rod is a short stick.

clue.text: Baker ordered firm to supply meal

indicators.note: the baker's letters are put in a new order

parts.note: fast means firmly fixed

explanation.surface: A baker was told to provide food for a company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' makes BREAK from BAKER; 'firm' looks like a company but means fixed.
explanation.definitionFit: The first meal of the day is one particular meal.

clue.text: Mishap caused by stress — I'd go into it

indicators.note: I'd is placed inside the word for stress

parts.note: an accent is a stress on a syllable
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something went wrong under strain, and someone volunteers to investigate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go into' reads as investigating the mishap, but it is the container signal; 'it' simply points back to the stress.
explanation.definitionFit: An unfortunate unplanned event is a mishap.

clue.text: Arrive with fresh request for admission

parts.note: to come is to arrive
clean means fresh, unsoiled

explanation.surface: Someone turns up with a new application to get in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admission' suggests entry, but here it is a confession.
explanation.definitionFit: Telling someone to confess everything is asking them to make an admission.

clue.text: He has broken links with one foreign capital

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the word links is broken up and reassembled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A man has cut his ties with a single overseas city.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Finland is a foreign capital to the setter.

clue.text: Stay second

definitions.meaning: a prop or brace that holds something up
to back a motion or a person

explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a physical prop, and to second is to back someone, both senses of the word.

clue.text: Officer in difficult situation turned to other ranks

indicators.note: turned means the word for a difficult situation is read backwards

parts.note: a jam is a tight spot
OR is the military abbreviation for other ranks

explanation.surface: An officer in a tight spot sought help from the enlisted soldiers.
explanation.definitionFit: A rank of army officer above captain.

clue.text: Carpenters likely to become union members?

definitions.meaning: people who sign up, as to a trade union

explanation.definitionFit: Woodworkers who make furniture share the name with people who sign up to things.

clue.text: Miss having a nap on Sunday

indicators.note: in an across answer, on means placed after the following piece

parts.note: kip is British slang for sleep, a nap

explanation.surface: Missing church because of a Sunday snooze.
explanation.definitionFit: To skip is to miss or omit something.

clue.text: It's cold in the country — you need a fur

indicators.note: the word for cold sits inside the country

parts.note: China is a country
chill means cold

explanation.surface: It is freezing in that country, so wrap up in fur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the country' looks generic but names CHINA.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft grey pelt of a small Andean rodent is a prized fur.

clue.text: Contents of many an ancient vessel

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral 100, many
the Argo was Jason's ship in Greek myth

explanation.surface: What was carried in old ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods carried aboard a ship are its contents.

clue.text: Language of a quarter of Parisians

parts.note: the Left Bank student district of Paris bears the name of the old scholarly tongue

explanation.surface: The tongue spoken by a fourth of the people of Paris.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a quarter' looks like a fraction but is a district of Paris named for the students' old tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: The classical tongue of ancient Rome is a language.

clue.text: Approves of indications of support

definitions.meaning: tokens such as rosettes worn to show allegiance

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means to prefer, and the noun means tokens like rosettes showing loyalty.

clue.text: They are said to be just barren areas

definitions.text: They are said to be just
definitions.meaning: what one deserves, from the idiom of getting what one merits
arid wildernesses such as the Sahara

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both what one has earned, as in the idiom, and arid wastelands.

clue.text: Can you beat it for personal adornment?

definitions.meaning: a drumbeat signalling soldiers back to quarters, which can be beaten
an inked design on the skin

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a drum signal and also an inked skin design.

clue.text: Unions strangely in agreement

indicators.note: the word unions is arranged in a strange new way

explanation.surface: Trade unions are oddly all on the same page.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting in harmony or simultaneously is a state of agreement.
